title: Keats's images
back: Bower, flowery band, pall; sun and moon, daffodils and rills, the endless fountain.

title: The argument of the lines
back: Joy for ever → gifts → flowery band → pall lifted → catalogue → endless fountain.

title: A joy for ever
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Beauty never passes into nothingness" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="160" cy="95" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="8"/><circle cx="160" cy="95" r="30" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="5"/><circle cx="160" cy="95" r="12" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><text x="160" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">its loveliness increases</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Beauty never passes into nothingness</text></svg>
back: Each return gives more; the joy stays and grows in memory. Beauty does not wear out like other pleasures.

title: The flowery band
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Woven every morning — against despondence and gloom" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="160" cy="100" r="60" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="10"/><circle cx="220.0" cy="100.0" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="189.85426287350361" cy="152.045393535641" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="129.70923372400856" cy="151.79256199893243" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="100.00007609634763" cy="100.0955591749892" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="130.58435071955805" cy="47.70545365518471" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="190.20824028412684" cy="48.159261010895534" r="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160" y="176" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">binds us to the earth</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Woven every morning — against despondence and gloom</text></svg>
back: Beauty is the garland that keeps us wanting to live despite despondence, the dearth of noble people, gloomy days and over-darkened ways.

title: Lifting the pall
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A funeral cloth over the spirit — moved away by some shape of beauty" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><rect x="60" y="110" width="200" height="60" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none" rx="4"/><path d="M60,110 Q160,40 260,110 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.3" stroke="none"/><circle cx="160" cy="60" r="22" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M160,100 L160,45 M164.8,53.8 L160,45 L155.2,53.8" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">A funeral cloth over the spirit — moved away by some shape of beauty</text></svg>
back: The pall covers a coffin; our gloom is a death-cloth on the soul. Any beautiful thing lifts it. The most-asked metaphor.

title: Sun, moon, trees, daffodils, rills, musk-rose
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Nature's small, sheltering beauties" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="60" cy="50" r="20" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M110,36 A14,14 0 1 0 110,64 A17.5,17.5 0 0 1 110,36 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><g><rect x="56.4" y="125.0" width="7.2" height="45.0" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/><circle cx="60" cy="107.0" r="27.0" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/><circle cx="43.8" cy="120.5" r="18.0" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/><circle cx="76.2" cy="120.5" r="18.0" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/></g><g transform="translate(150,172) scale(1.0)"><path d="M0,0 V-60" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M0,-60 Q-10.799999999999999,-64.8 -18,-68 Q-7.2,-69.6 0,-60 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M0,-60 Q10.799999999999999,-64.8 18,-68 Q7.2,-69.6 0,-60 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M0,-60 Q-7.199999999999999,-51.6 -12,-46 Q-4.800000000000001,-43.2 0,-60 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M0,-60 Q7.199999999999999,-51.6 12,-46 Q4.800000000000001,-43.2 0,-60 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M0,-60 Q0.0,-72.0 0,-80 Q0.0,-84.0 0,-60 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="0" cy="-60" r="6" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/></g><path d="M190,165 q10.0,-6 20.0,0 q10.0,6 20.0,0 q10.0,-6 20.0,0 q10.0,6 20.0,0 q10.0,-6 20.0,0 q10.0,6 20.0,0" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" opacity="0.8"/><circle cx="250" cy="120" r="14" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Nature's small, sheltering beauties</text></svg>
back: Shade for simple sheep, a cooling covert against the hot season, blooms deep in the forest brake — every image gives shelter or refreshment.

title: An endless fountain of immortal drink
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Why the joy lasts: its source is heavenly and never runs dry" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><path d="M100,165 H220 L210,185 H110 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><rect x="154" y="95" width="12" height="70" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M160,95 Q130,55 100,155" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M160,95 Q145,55 130,155" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M160,95 Q175,55 190,155" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M160,95 Q190,55 220,155" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M160,95 V50" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></g><text x="160" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">from heaven's brink</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Why the joy lasts: its source is heavenly and never runs dry</text></svg>
back: The closing image answers the opening line. Beauty is divine nectar, inexhaustible, giving a kind of immortality.

title: Beauty beyond nature
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Line to remember" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><rect x="28" y="36" width="264" height="72" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/><path d="M50,108 L42,122 L64,108 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="68.05" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">the grandeur of the dooms</text><text x="160.0" y="85.05" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">of the mighty dead</text></g><text x="160" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">— and all lovely tales we have heard or read</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Line to remember</text></svg>
back: Heroic lives and noble deaths of the past, and literature itself, are things of beauty too. Include them in the catalogue answer.
